grammar.medium: Flat night-lithograph SVG per identity.json draft: solid ink slabs, 2-3 flat hues per plate + lamp color, converging-line perspective, beams as flat wedges, lamps as flat discs with hard 2px halo rings. NEVER glow, NEVER gradients, NEVER gold. Linework >= 2px at final size.
grammar.green_logic: Part I = green/clear: the Line still runs; the world has not yet voted to stop. Every plate carries exactly one green function (lamp, lamp pair, bracelet-clasp disc, gantry row, furnace lamp, truss lamp, headlight wedge edge, vault-lamp, flame-base signal) — never decoration. Brass/glow/gold explicitly refused (A2): copper appears ONLY as flat Railsteel-warm slab in p1c5, capped at one plate.
grammar.intruder_policy: ONE intruder: p1c10 carries signal-stop-intruder (red lamp on a green part) exactly as identity.json documents — Wyatt's Torch is the Line's first death. Red appears nowhere else in Part I, NOT even in the p1c1 broken-signal red (rendered as a dead dark disc, lamp OUT) or the p1c4 Alliance vote (lamps shuttered, no red lit). The identity's other intruders (p3c1, p3c10) are untouched.
grammar.no_index_correlation: Plate weights and motifs authored per chapter from para counts + verified scenes, never computed from chapter index. No odd/even alternation. Monumental: p1c7. Grand: p1c5, p1c6, p1c9, p1c10. Standard: p1c1, p1c4, p1c8. Compact: p1c2, p1c3. (Weights propose two moves from the identity sketch — p1c1 standard-down, p1c8 standard-down — justified per entry; supervisor decides.)

p1c1.title: THE THEME
p1c1.rationale: Opens on the bum's question 'Who is John Galt?' (:0) and Eddie's dread (:9), then the three verified anchors: the sky-calendar page (:12), the oak tree memory (:18-20, hollow trunk 'like the mouth of a black tunnel' :20), and the faded Taggart wall map with red lines 'like a system of blood vessels' (:34). Middle: Dagny's night ride on the Taggart Comet (:142), the stall at the book's FIRST red signal — busted, waited on for an hour in placid indifference (:148-160: 'I think it's busted' :158, 'Waiting for it to change' :160) — her order 'Proceed with caution to the next signal' (:180), and the tunnel descent into the Terminal (:205-206, with 'green and red lights hung as distant drops of color' specifically at :206). Closes on Kellogg's quitting and the returned question (:390-404). The plate fuses the chapter's two signal moments — the dead red in the fields and the live drops in the tunnel — into the book's first signal grammar statement; the oak/calendar/map triptych stays prose, not art, to keep one huge idea per plate.
p1c1.proposed_motif: Two stacked planes in one plate. UPPER plane (fields at night): the Comet's motionless wheel-line as a black slab, crew figures as small dark verticals, and above them the broken signal rendered as a DARK dead disc — lamp OUT, no red lit anywhere (intruder discipline). LOWER plane (the Terminal tunnels): converging rail-lines head-on into black holes, with green lamps as flat discs + hard 2px halo rings and the reds left dark. One green function only: the tunnel drops. The plate's argument: the Line runs where men act (Dagny :180), and stops where they wait (:146-149).
p1c1.palette_role: Clear Green (#3FD08C) carries ONLY the tunnel lamp-drops; the dead signal disc is unlit Tunnelblack (#07090C) ringed Railsteel (#8B98A5); wheel-line and crew in flat dark slabs on Nightballast (#0E1216); plate whites minimal (Headlight #F2E8D0 for a single beam edge). No red, no amber: the chapter's red is DEATH, and death stays unlit until p1c10.
p1c1.opener_idea: STANDARD band (9rem). Plate: dead-disc fields over lit-drops tunnels. Kicker: PART I · NON-CONTRADICTION (Space Mono, green). Head: THE THEME (Barlow Condensed 600). p1c2.title: THE CHAIN
p1c2.rationale: Opens on the night approach to the Rearden mills (:0-2): scattered lights, the steam-wrapped buildings, 'a few strong lights cut straight sheafs through the coils' (:2). Middle: the first pour of Rearden Metal — the tap-hole break as 'a shocking sensation of morning' (:9), the white stream with 'fountains of sparks shot in beating spasms, as from broken arteries' (:9) — and Rearden's walk home fingering the bracelet 'made of Rearden Metal, in the shape of a chain' (:17), made from 'that first poured metal' (:29), ten years in the making (:17). Closes on Lillian raising the bracelet in the lamplight (:212): 'A chain... the chain by which he holds us all in bondage' (:213). Shortest Part I chapter (214 paras). The plate stages the pour, not the insult: the metal's birth is the chapter; the bondage line is its caption's shadow.
p1c2.proposed_motif: The furnace at night as a single black bulk; from its tap-hole a flat Headlight wedge of white metal streaming down (beam-vocabulary, never a glow), edged with a few flat spark-dashes struck at the wedge's rim — NO red sparks, NO orange: the text's 'pure white color of sunlight' (:9) is a white-on-black image. ONE green function: a small green lamp disc on the furnace housing (the Line's order for this metal — the rails of :28). In the plate's lower corner, small and separate: the bracelet as a flat chain-link loop, clasp open. Two scales, one metal: the tonnage and the gift.
p1c2.palette_role: Headlight (#F2E8D0) does structural graphic work: the white metal wedge is the plate's brightest plane (explicit beam-vocabulary exception, same license as Part II's p2c3). Clear Green carries ONLY the furnace lamp disc. Furnace bulk Tunnelblack wrapped in Railsteel tube-coils on Nightballast. No red/orange flame tints anywhere — the pour is white or it is wrong.

p1c3.title: THE TOP AND THE BOTTOM
p1c3.rationale: Opens on the cellar sixty floors up: the low vaulted room (:0) where Boyle, Taggart, Larkin and Mouch plot in whispers (:1-11) — the TOP that behaves as a cellar. Middle: Dagny's night crossing of the Taggart concourse, 'like a temple' with 'dim vaults' and 'giant granite columns' (:215), dominated by the statue of Nathaniel Taggart, 'the only form of prayer she knew' (:216), Nat as the man 'who had never accepted the creed that others had the right to stop him' (:218). Closes in the underground cafeteria (:243-248): white tile 'like silver brocade' (:244), Eddie confessing the Rio Norte hope to the track worker (:246-248). The chapter's architecture is a vertical argument — cellar-above vs. temple-below — and the plate draws exactly that section. HONEST FLAG on the identity sketch ('Nat Taggart statue + Comet'): confirmed — full-text scan finds ZERO 'comet' hits in this chapter (the census hit was a substring false positive); the Comet runs in p1c1 :142. The sketch's Comet is resisted. This draft substitutes the concourse vault + statue, both verified here.
p1c3.proposed_motif: An architectural SECTION plate, split horizontally. UPPER third (the 'top'): the cellar-room vault as a low dark arch pressing down, four seated slabs around a small table under a single DEAD (unlit) fixture — the plotters get no lamp. LOWER two-thirds (the 'bottom' that is the true top): the concourse vaults rising on granite column-slabs, and at the vanishing point the small upright figure of the Nat Taggart statue. ONE green function: a single green lamp disc hung at the concourse vanishing point behind the statue — the Line's promise, kept below. The section line between the worlds drawn as a hard Headlight hairline: the chapter's whole thesis in one cut.
p1c3.palette_role: Clear Green carries ONLY the concourse vanishing-point lamp; the cellar fixture stays dark (Railsteel ring, Tunnelblack disc). Cellar arch near-total Tunnelblack; concourse columns flat Railsteel slabs on Nightballast; the section hairline Headlight (#F2E8D0). The palette stages the title: darkness above, structure below.

p1c4.title: THE IMMOVABLE MOVERS
p1c4.rationale: Opens on Dagny's axiom: 'Motive power... movement, to keep it immovable' (:0) under the Taggart Building, then the rotted precision machine tool abandoned in the yard (:2) and McNamara's quitting (:5-11). Middle: the Halley Fourth on the phonograph — 'a great cry of rebellion' (:34) — against the loudspeaker's shapeless screech (:26); the Mexico nationalization decree (:89) and Taggart's lying Board speech (:90-93); the National Alliance vote where 'everybody looked at Dan Conway' (:127) and the hall fell silent after the Anti-dog-eat-dog Rule passed (:128). Closes on the Rearden-Dagny mountain-top exchange (:323-331): 'it's we who move the world' (:331). The plate takes the vote — the chapter's hinge — rendered as signal hardware: the Alliance DOES what a dwarf signal does (holds one road, clears another). HONEST FLAG on the identity sketch ('stalled boardroom as dwarf signal, red-over-green'): confirmed — NO dwarf hardware, NO red-over-green aspects in the text (full-text scan: 'signal' occurs only as the chairman's hand-raise :127 and a trackside memory :181). The Alliance-vote-as-signal reading is this draft's STRUCTURAL metaphor (the vote holds one road, clears another), rendered with shuttered lamps + ONE lit green and the stopped aspect as an unlit dark disc — the hardware is grammar, not illustration, and the file asserts nothing stronger. (The chapter's other verified set-pieces — the Rearden rail-order meeting :214-320 and the crane-magnet rail-loading :304-312 — stay prose so the plate keeps one huge idea.)

p1c6.title: THE NON-COMMERCIAL
p1c6.rationale: Opens on Rearden's mirror (:0-8): the anniversary party as duty, the Equalization editorial (:11-12) predicting the bill 'forbidding any pe[rson]...' (:12), Mouch's reassurance (:13). Middle: the party as a bestiary — Dr. Pritchett's 'nothing is anything' (:185) and pro-bill catechism (:40), Scudder's 'Property rights are a superstition' (:100), Philip's Friends of Global Progress (:94), Eubank's subsidy plea (:180) — broken by Francisco's arrival and the Rearden confrontation: 'I came to this party solely in order to meet you' (:259), 'What are you trying to do?' (:297) / 'I am calling your attention to the nature of those for whom you are working' (:298), 'Why are you willing to carry them?' (:300), 'the aim of all their efforts is to keep you from knowing it' (:305). Closes on the marriage's cold ledger (:492-501): 'What did she want from him?... there was no answer' (:501). The chapter's other hinge is the bracelet-for-diamonds exchange: Dagny hears Lillian exhibiting the metal bracelet (:443-444), tears off her own diamond band — 'If you are not the coward that I think you are, you will exchange it' (:445-446) — and takes the metal (:452-454) under the mangled Halley (:439-441, :450). The plate takes the party room as a signal gantry — the chandelier inverted into hardware — with the exchange honored in the motif's clasp detail; the pour-sketch is refused (verified: 'pour' occurs 3× only as 'poured' slime :162, 'pouring a ton of steel' metaphor :241, and a memory :484 — NO rail-pour scene; the set-piece first pour is p1c2 :7-9). HONEST FLAG on the identity sketch ('wedding of steel — first Rearden Metal rail pour'): NO pour occurs in this chapter (the pours are p1c2 :7-9 and the p1c7 rail-pour :692); the chapter is a drawing-room, and forcing a furnace plate onto it would lie. This draft renders the verified room.
p1c6.proposed_motif: The Rearden drawing room at night as a signal-gantry plate: the party crowd as a row of small dark seated/standing slabs along the plate's bottom third (NO faces, NO caricature — the text's contempt is philosophical, and the plate refuses cartooning), and above them the chandelier drawn as an INVERTED SIGNAL GANTRY spanning the full plate width: a black crossbar carrying a row of small lamps. The row's discipline is the image: all lamps DARK except ONE green disc burning at the gantry's far end — Francisco's position in the room (:259-305), the single live mind under the fixture. ONE green function: that end disc. Flat discs + hard halo ring on the lit one; dark discs ringed Railsteel. At the plate's bottom edge, small and exact: two open bracelet-loops side by side — one flat Headlight diamond-band, one green-blue metal chain-loop (:452-454) — clasps open, mid-exchange. The loops are drawn, not labeled; the gantry stays the plate's one huge idea.

p1c7.title: THE EXPLOITERS AND THE EXPLOITED
p1c7.rationale: Opens on the Wyatt grade: 'The rails rose through the rocks to the oil derricks and the oil derricks rose to the sky' (:0), the green-blue rails across the bridge (:1-2), the fifteen-hundred-foot gorge (:5), the sparkling switches (:6). Middle: the notebook truss — 'a single twelve-hundred-foot-truss span' of a new type (:99), 'Rearden Truss' (:821) — drawn up on 'a pile of frozen lumber' (:99); the poured-steel glow crossing Rearden's desk (:360, :639); the last rail for the John Galt Line being poured (:692); the looters' laws closing in (Rearden Ore sign :810). Closes on the truss-with-arch invention: the midnight drawing session (:819-820) and the phone call — 'throw in the ashcan all the drawings I sent you... combining a truss with an arch... carry four trains at once, stand three hundred years' (:821-822). Longest Part I chapter (823 paras, 25,618 words). The plate is the bridge — the book's longest plate for its longest span.
p1c7.proposed_motif: The bridge as a MONUMENTAL night span: a twelve-hundred-foot truss-and-arch drawn in flat Railsteel line-work (linework >= 2px at final size) arcing across the FULL plate width over a Tunnelblack gorge cut, green-blue rails (:1) picked out as two thin Headlight lines riding the span. ONE green function: a single green lamp disc hung at the span's crown — the Line's own light, earned by the drawing (:819-822). Below the span, in the gorge dark: the dry river bed's boulders as flat slabs (:5). At the plate's right abutment, tiny: two seated figures on lumber (:99) — the notebook scene, human scale against the span. No furnace, no pour: the bridge is the chapter, and it fills the plate edge to edge.

p1c9.title: THE SACRED AND THE PROFANE
p1c9.rationale: Opens on the Venetian-blind bands: 'glowing bands on the skin of her arm, spaced like bracelets' (:0), the mechanic 'in the stripes of sunlight and shadow, like a convict behind bars' (:5) — bars that 'were not bars any longer' but 'cracks of a wall which the John Galt Line had broken' (:5).
